title: 5.8 A 20W CMOS/LDMOS All-Digital Transmitter with Dynamic Retiming and Glitch-Free Phase Mapper, Achieving 68%/62% Peak Drain/System Efficiency
problem: Base stations dominate wireless operator energy consumption (73%); analog PA-based transmitters suffer from high quiescent currents and limited bandwidth, but achieving high-power all-digital transmitters (DTX) at mMIMO levels (>3W) requires fine gate segmentation and glitch-free operation for wideband modulation.
motivation: All-digital transmitters offer substantial energy savings through switching operation and zero quiescent currents; enabling high-power (>3W), high-efficiency DTX reduces base-station energy consumption critically.
method: 8-phase multi-phase digital upconversion transmitter with dynamic retiming and glitch-free phase-mapper; custom low-VT LDMOS MMIC with power switch banks featuring in-finger gate segmentation and high-density flip-chip DTX controller integration.
key_novelty: First all-digital transmitter achieving mMIMO power levels (20W integrated) with wideband modulation support through dynamic retiming and glitch-free phase mapping, demonstrating DTX viability for base-station deployment.
contributions: 8-phase multi-phase (MP) digital upconversion architecture with dynamic retiming
Glitch-free phase-mapper enabling wideband modulated signal support
High-density flip-chip DTX implementation with custom low-VT LDMOS MMIC
In-finger gate segmentation for fine output power resolution and 20W integrated power

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 68% peak drain efficiency, 62% peak system efficiency

baselines: Analog PA-based transmitters, prior DTX designs limited to <3W
limitations: Detailed bandwidth, latency, and thermal characteristics not discussed; comparison with state-of-the-art base-station PA solutions not provided.
primary_theme: High-power all-digital transmitter for energy-efficient base stations
